newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, December off 6 pct on week.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, December off 6 pct on week.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures edged lower on Friday, rounding out a week of sharp losses in which the market pulled back six percent from recent highs.

In its fifth straight negative close, benchmark December coffee fell 0.80 cent per lb on the day, to 109.10 cents. An early bout of speculative and producer-linked selling pushed December to 108.50, a key support level, but scale-down trade and commission house buying helped pare the losses.
"The market ran into some support at the lows, and there was some light short covering," said one trader.
Top-grower Brazil was a notably steady seller on the day, emerging after several days on the sidelines to lock in prices on its current harvest.
"Brazil hit the panic button, they have a big crop to sell," the trader added.
Price-fixing by origin countries was also expected to cap the upside next week, dealers said, citing news Colombia would open December coffee registrations on October 21.
Traders said this week's steep seven-cent reversal was somewhat at odds with the current fundamental picture, in which U.S. inventories running at their lowest level in a decade.
But they added that with fresh Latin American supply expected to flood the consumer market in the next month or so, roasters maintained a cautious buying stance.
Technically, traders said December's ability to hold above 108.00 sent a constructive signal, but many reckoned the market would likely take aim at nearby support levels early next week.

Sell stops were believed widely placed under the 107.25-106.50 range, while stiff resistance was noted at around 112.00-112.10 cents. Traders were also keeping an eye on the volatile December-March switch, which widened out to 9.00 cents this week before narrowing back to 7.55 on Friday.
An estimated 5,875 lots were exchanged Friday, with the bulk of the day's transactions recorded during the first two hours of trading.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
